articles.title: Kenya: Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) - Key Findings from the 2026 Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessment (June 2026)
articles.description: Please refer to the attached file. Publication: October 2026 - Data Collection: June 2026 KEY MESSAGES Needs remained widespread across assessed households: 97% were classified as being in need according to the 2026 Multi-Sectoral Needs Index (MSNI), including 59% in severe need. Unrestricted cash was the most preferred assistance modality, selected as a first preference by 75% of households, followed by in-kind food (17%). Households mainly expected assistance to address food-related needs, access to safe drinking water and lack of income. Overall, 48% of assessed households reported receiving humanitarian assistance in the 12 months prior to data collection. Among recipient households, 58% reported receiving unrestricted cash. More than half (58%) of households felt that assistance reached those most in need CONTEXT Kenya’s arid and semi-arid lands (ASALs) entered 2026 under continued humanitarian pressure following the below-average and erratic October–December 2025 short rains. Poor rainfall contributed to crop losses, limited pasture regeneration and livestock losses. By early 2026, approximately 3.3 million people were estimated to be food insecure, with high needs reported in Mandera, Wajir, Garissa, Turkana and Marsabit. Although the March–May long rains improved water and pasture conditions, depleted herds, previous livelihood losses and high costs continued to constrain household recovery. Refugee households faced distinct pressures. As of August 2026, Kenya hosted close to one million refugees and asylum-seekers, mainly in Dadaab, Kakuma and Kalobeyei. Limited livelihoods, reliance on humanitarian assistance, and changes in aid policy and targeting constrained households’ ability to meet basic needs. Food security is one example of these wider challenges, with recent IPC findings estimating that around 351,000 refugees were facing Crisis or worse acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 3 or above). With needs remaining high and resources constrained, understanding households’ experiences and preferences is important. This factsheet examines assistance receipt, adequacy, preferred modalities, perceived targeting and reported difficulties associated with assistance.
